name: Bordeaux Cathedral
description: A Gothic cathedral with a separate bell tower, where Eleanor of Aquitaine married the future King Louis VII of France in 1137.

name: Palais de Justice
description: The neoclassical courthouse where the Vichy official Maurice Papon was tried in 1997 and 1998 for the deportation of Jews.

name: Grand Théâtre
description: An opera house from 1780 with twelve columns across its front, on a square at the center of the city.

name: Musée du Vin et du Négoce
places: Musée du Vin et du Négoce, Chartrons
description: A museum of the wine trade in the cellars of an 18th-century merchant’s house in the Chartrons quarter.

name: Place des Quinconces
places: Statue of Montaigne, Place des Quinconces
description: One of the largest squares in Europe, with a tall monument to the Girondins, a group of revolutionaries, and statues of two writers.

name: Statue of Aristides de Sousa Mendes
places: Statue of Aristides de Sousa Mendes
description: A statue of the Portuguese consul who issued thousands of visas to refugees in Bordeaux in June 1940.

name: Place de la Bourse
description: An 18th-century square of classical buildings facing the river, with a shallow reflecting pool laid out in front in 2006.
